```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from here: into this
# document, and into whatever else needs it, which reads the errata_entries.csv written at
# the bottom of this file rather than keeping a second hand-typed copy.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here, \was{} in an edition. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be
# set by either.
#
# Numbering is APPEND-ONLY once this note is published: an entry can already have been
# cited, so a later finding is added at the end and never interleaved.
#
# claim_ids is empty throughout, since no entry corrects a printed number.
#
# Entry 11 is a note (decision 15): it corrects nothing, so its corrected field is NA.
#
# Every quotation was checked against an image of the published page on 2026-11-05, and
# entry 12's on 2026-11-06. The
# years in entries 4, 5, and 7 come from Crossref, read the same day.
#
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, carrying
# the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. The sentence already holds
# it, but only inside prose a reader has to parse. Each value comes from the same expression
# that glues the sentence, so the two cannot be written apart, and the gate below re-checks
# that each one is still inside the span it belongs to. An entry of a class that changes no
# quantity carries NA, and so does a note-form entry, which corrects nothing.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  3, "bibliographic", "reading", "brief",
  "The An et al. citation names the authors by their given names",

  NA_character_,

(Imai 2008; Mcconnell, Stuart, and Devaney 2008; Lee [[2010]]). ... and Lee ([[2010]]). ... and Lee ([[2010]]) ... Imbens and Manski (2004) and Lee ([[2010]])",
  "Lee, David S. [[2009]]. Training, wages, and sample selection: Estimating sharp bounds on treatment effects. Review of Economic Studies 76(3):1071–1102. ... (Imai 2008; Mcconnell, Stuart, and Devaney 2008; Lee [[2009]]). ... and Lee ([[2009]]). ... and Lee ([[2009]]) ... Imbens and Manski (2004) and Lee ([[2009]])",
  "Crossref, doi 10.1111/j.1467-937x.2009.00536.x, gives volume 76, issue 3, pages 1071 to 1102, issued July 2009. The printed volume and pages are those of the 2009 issue. The p. 188 citation's \"Mcconnell\" is corrected in entry 6, and the p. 195 citation of Zhang and Rubin in entry 5.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  5, "bibliographic", "reading", "brief",
  "The Zhang and Rubin reference and its citation give the year as 2004",
  "published p. 206, the reference list, and the citation on p. 195",
  "Zhang, Junni L., and Donald B. Rubin. [[2004]]. Estimation of causal effects via principal stratification when some outcomes are truncated by 'death'. Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics 28(4):353–368. ... See Manski (1990, 1995, 2007), Zhang and Rubin ([[2004]]), and Lee (2010)",
  "Zhang, Junni L., and Donald B. Rubin. [[2003]]. Estimation of causal effects via principal stratification when some outcomes are truncated by 'death'. Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics 28(4):353–368. ... See Manski (1990, 1995, 2007), Zhang and Rubin ([[2003]]), and Lee (2010)",
  "Crossref, doi 10.3102/10769986028004353, gives volume 28, issue 4, pages 353 to 368, issued December 2003. The p. 195 sentence also cites Lee, corrected in entry 4.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  6, "spelling", "reading", "brief",
  "\"Mcconnell\" for \"McConnell\"",
  "published p. 188, footnote 1",
  "(Imai 2008; [[Mcconnell]], Stuart, and Devaney 2008; Lee 2010).",
  "(Imai 2008; [[McConnell]], Stuart, and Devaney 2008; Lee 2010).",
  "The reference list on p. 205 spells the name correctly. The year of the Lee citation is corrected in entry 4.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  8, "spelling", "reading", "brief",
  "\"assuption\" for \"assumption\"",
  "published appendix p. 3, Section 2",
  "In this section we present analyses under an [[assuption]] that missingness is independent of potential outcomes",
  "In this section we present analyses under an [[assumption]] that missingness is independent of potential outcomes",
  "",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  9, "wording", "reading", "brief",
  "A dropped article in appendix Section 2",
  "published appendix p. 3, Section 2",
  "We observe strong average effect of the Polarized treatment on Perceived Polarization in Wave 1 (0.468 points).",
  "We observe [[a]] strong average effect of the Polarized treatment on Perceived Polarization in Wave 1 (0.468 points).",
  "",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  "bring in something [[fresh and]] the new format really has done that. ... and wanting to show what they can [[do because]] they have the chance to do what it is that they do. ... in many different [[packages whether]] it be color, creed, size, [[anything because]] you get to see these people",
  "Each pair most likely lost a punctuation mark between its two words when the appendix was typeset. The source text is not in the replication archive, so the correction supplies only the space and restores no punctuation.",

  "Si, Yajuan, Jerome P. Reiter, and D. Sunshine Hillygus. [[2015]]. Semi-parametric selection models for potentially non-ignorable attrition in panel studies with refreshment samples. Political Analysis 23(1):92–112. ... Si, Reiter, and Hillygus [[2015]]),",
  "Crossref, doi 10.1093/pan/mpu009, gives volume 23, issue 1, pages 92 to 112, issued 2015. The printed volume and pages are those of the 2015 issue.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  11, "wording", "reading", "note",
  "A probable stray word in the Moderate stimulus",
  "published appendix p. 5, Section 4.1",
  "While he supports gay marriage, he did not push to change federal [[on]] policy on this issue, knowing that it might upset some voters.",
  NA,
  "The sentence reads as \"to change federal policy on this issue\" with a stray \"on\". The appendix reproduces the stimulus that subjects read, and we have not been able to check the fielded instrument, so we do not correct it: if the slip was in the text subjects saw, the appendix reports it faithfully.",
  "",
  NA_character_,

  12, "typographical", "reading", "brief",
  "A stray space inside a citation",
  "published p. 203, Section 5",
  "ignorable conditional on observables [[( Little]] and Rubin 2002, ch. 15).",
  "ignorable conditional on observables [[(Little]] and Rubin 2002, ch. 15).",
  "",
  "",
  NA_character_
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values),
                as.character)) |>
  arrange(entry)

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry),
          all(is.na(entries$corrected) == (entries$form == "note")))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and
# its spans outnumber its values.
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values)) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, \(v, s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none may
# not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds. A note-form
# entry corrects nothing, so it carries NA whatever its class. An empty claim_ids is stored
# as "" and counts as missing here.
has_ids <- !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & entries$claim_ids != ""
needs_value <- entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" & has_ids
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[needs_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[!needs_value])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | has_ids)
)

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document. Another renderer resolves it differently.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, which is why every emitted
# entry opens with one.
emit_entry <- function(n) {
  e <- entries |> filter(entry == n)
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ",
      str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ", bold(e$published), sep = "")
  if (e$form != "note") cat("\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), sep = "")
  if (nzchar(e$note)) cat("\n\n", e$note, sep = "")
  cat("\n")
}
```

This note lists `r sum(entries$form != "note")` corrections and one unresolved wording question in "Combining Double Sampling and Bounds to Address Nonignorable Missing Outcomes in Randomized Experiments," published in *Political Analysis* 25(2):188--206, doi [10.1017/pan.2016.6](https://doi.org/10.1017/pan.2016.6), and its online appendix. **None of them changes an estimate or a conclusion of the paper.** In the article, one sentence gives the size of two arms as the size of the whole experiment, and Table 1's column headings misplace two columns. Four are citations: one prints its authors' given names in place of their surnames, and three give the wrong year. The rest are a misspelled name in a citation and, in the appendix, a misspelling, a dropped article, and words run together in a treatment stimulus. The last item flags a probable stray word in a stimulus without correcting it.

All were found by reading the article and its appendix word by word, and each quotation was checked against an image of the published page. The years were checked against the Crossref record named in each entry's note, and the arm sizes in entry 1 against the deposited replication archive, doi [10.7910/DVN/AQB4MP](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/AQB4MP). The code supporting the maintained analysis is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_etal_2017](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_etal_2017).

# The article

```{r article-entries, results="asis"}
walk(1:2, emit_entry)
```

# Citations and the reference list

```{r citation-entries, results="asis"}
walk(3:7, emit_entry)
```

# The appendix

```{r appendix-entries, results="asis"}
walk(8:11, emit_entry)
```

# The article, continued

```{r article-continued-entries, results="asis"}
walk(12, emit_entry)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else
# that needs these entries reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot
# drift.
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
